note: General guidance for academic/demo use. Always follow the product label and confirm with a local agriculture officer (in India: Krishi Vigyan Kendra / state agriculture department) before spraying.

classes.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves that turn dark and scabby; infected leaves yellow and drop early; corky scabs on fruit.
chemical: Protectant sprays of captan or mancozeb from green-tip stage through petal fall
Myclobutanil (systemic) in wet springs
organic: Sulfur or lime-sulfur sprays before rain periods
prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn
Prune to open the canopy for air flow

classes.symptoms: 'Frog-eye' leaf spots: tan centres with purple margins; rotting fruit that turns black and mummifies; sunken cankers on branches.
chemical: Captan or thiophanate-methyl sprays during the growing season
organic: Prune out cankers and dead wood 15 cm below the infection
prevention: Remove mummified fruit from tree and ground
Avoid bark wounds; keep trees vigorous

classes.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface, later with small tube-like structures on the underside; fruit may be deformed.
chemical: Myclobutanil or mancozeb from pink bud stage to petal fall
organic: Remove orange galls from nearby juniper/cedar trees
prevention: Avoid planting junipers close to apple trees

classes.symptoms: White powdery patches on young leaves and shoots; leaves curl upward and may become brittle.
chemical: Myclobutanil or wettable sulfur at first sign

classes.symptoms: Rectangular tan to grey lesions running parallel between leaf veins; lesions merge and blight whole leaves.
chemical: Strobilurin (azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin) or triazole (propiconazole) fungicide around tasseling when disease is spreading
prevention: Avoid continuous maize in humid areas

classes.symptoms: Small, cinnamon-brown powdery pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces.
chemical: Mancozeb or propiconazole if infection appears early and spreads quickly
organic: Usually tolerable on field corn; remove heavily infected leaves in small plots
prevention: Sow early to avoid peak rust weather

classes.symptoms: Long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions, 2.5–15 cm long, starting on lower leaves.
chemical: Propiconazole or azoxystrobin around tasseling if lesions reach upper leaves

classes.symptoms: Circular tan leaf spots with dark borders and tiny black dots; berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
chemical: Mancozeb, captan or myclobutanil from early shoot growth through 4 weeks after bloom
organic: Remove all mummified berries and infected canes
prevention: Clean up vineyard debris before spring

classes.symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' yellow/red patches between leaf veins that dry out; dark spots on berries; internal wood decay; sudden vine collapse.
chemical: No curative spray; protect fresh pruning wounds with a fungicidal wound sealant
organic: Cut out and burn infected wood

classes.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on older leaves that merge; leaves dry and fall early.
chemical: Mancozeb or copper oxychloride sprays

classes.pathogen: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, spread by Asian citrus psyllid
classes.symptoms: Blotchy, asymmetric yellow mottling of leaves; small, lopsided, bitter fruit that stays green; twig dieback.
chemical: No cure. Control the psyllid vector with insecticides recommended by your local agriculture office
organic: Remove and destroy infected trees to protect the orchard
Neem oil sprays against psyllid nymphs
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock
Report suspected cases to the agriculture department

classes.symptoms: Small angular purple-brown spots that drop out leaving 'shot holes'; yellowing leaves; cracked spots on fruit.
chemical: Fixed copper sprays at leaf fall and before bud break

classes.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn brown with yellow halos; leaves drop; raised scabby spots on fruit.
chemical: Copper hydroxide combined with mancozeb, every 7–10 days in wet weather

classes.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric 'target' rings and yellow halos, starting on older lower leaves.
chemical: Mancozeb, chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin at 7–10 day intervals

classes.symptoms: Large water-soaked dark lesions, white mould on the underside in humid weather; plants collapse within days; tubers rot.
chemical: Preventive mancozeb; once seen, metalaxyl + mancozeb or cymoxanil + mancozeb
organic: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
prevention: Hill up soil to protect tubers

classes.symptoms: White powdery spots on leaves and stems that spread to cover the leaf; leaves yellow and die.
chemical: Wettable sulfur or myclobutanil
organic: Diluted milk spray (1 part milk : 9 parts water)

classes.symptoms: Many small irregular purple blotches; centres dry so the leaf looks burnt or scorched.
chemical: Captan or myclobutanil during flowering and after harvest

classes.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves, often with yellow halos; scabby spots on fruit.
chemical: Copper hydroxide + mancozeb sprays

classes.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves, surrounded by yellow tissue; stem lesions near soil.
chemical: Mancozeb, chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin every 7–10 days

classes.symptoms: Large greasy grey-green to brown patches, white mould under leaves in humid weather; brown firm rot on fruit; rapid spread.
chemical: Metalaxyl + mancozeb or cymoxanil + mancozeb as soon as seen

classes.symptoms: Pale yellow spots on the upper leaf surface with olive-green velvety mould underneath; common in greenhouses.
chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb
organic: Improve ventilation and keep humidity below 85%

classes.symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and grey centres containing tiny black dots; lower leaves first.
chemical: Chlorothalonil or mancozeb

classes.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling on leaves, bronzing, and fine webbing on the underside; leaves dry up.
chemical: Miticides such as abamectin or spiromesifen (rotate chemistry to avoid resistance)
organic: Strong water spray on leaf undersides
prevention: Avoid drought stress and dusty conditions

classes.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings and light centres that may crack; spots on fruit near the stem.
chemical: Chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin

classes.pathogen: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (Begomovirus), spread by whitefly Bemisia tabaci
classes.symptoms: Leaves curl upward and become small with yellow margins; plants stunted; flowers drop.
chemical: No cure. Control whiteflies with recommended insecticides (e.g. imidacloprid, pyriproxyfen) per local label

classes.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic mottling, distorted or fern-like leaves, stunted growth.
chemical: No chemical cure
organic: Disinfect tools and hands (soap, or 10% bleach for tools)
prevention: Do not use tobacco near plants
